clue.text: Bishop engaging one craftsman involved with two parties

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so the bishop's letters take in the numeral

parts.note: BP is the standard abbreviation for bishop
one is the Roman numeral I
an artisan is a skilled craftsman

explanation.surface: A churchman takes on a tradesman in some cross-party venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with two parties' reads as gossip about the craftsman, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-party agreement or committee draws support from both sides of a two-party system.

clue.text: Cut beef spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of says the word for beef is heard rather than written

parts.note: to beef is to complain or grumble, i.e. to moan

explanation.surface: A butcher's instruction about slicing meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like meat but is the verb meaning complain.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass that has been mowed has been cut; the past participle matches 'Cut'.

clue.text: Friendly feelings you'd hope to get from a solicitor?

definitions.text: Friendly feelings you'd hope to get from a solicitor?

parts.words: Friendly feelings you'd hope to get from a solicitor?
parts.note: kindly benevolence, read as two words: a solicitor drafts a testament, and you hope it is a sound one

explanation.surface: Wishing for some kindness from one's lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Benevolent disposition towards others is the ordinary sense; split, it is a well-drafted testament.

clue.text: Secure TV presenter

definitions.meaning: to fix firmly in place, as a ship is held by its heavy weight on the seabed
the main newsreader linking a broadcast, especially in US usage

explanation.surface: A newsreader who has a safe job.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the verb to fasten firmly and the noun for a lead news broadcaster.

clue.text: Disheartened South Indian is bottom

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a Tamil is a person from Tamil Nadu in southern India

explanation.surface: A dejected man from southern India is at his lowest point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' removes M, the middle letter of TAMIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail is the rear or lowest end of something, so a synonym for bottom.

clue.text: Cut glass by sink that's falling into ruin

indicators.note: cut here means shortened, so the last letter of the drinking vessel is dropped

parts.note: a tumbler is a drinking glass
to sink is to go down

explanation.surface: Cut glass placed by a sink in some dilapidated house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut glass' reads as a craft term, but 'Cut' trims TUMBLER to TUMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilapidated building is said to be falling into ruin, crumbling with neglect.

clue.text: Audience's becoming more cheerful getting flashy stuff

indicators.note: an audience hears things, so the word for becoming cheerful is taken as heard

parts.note: a mood that is lifting is lightening

explanation.surface: A crowd perks up at a showy display.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical discharges in a storm come as flashes, a playful description of the weather phenomenon.

clue.text: Bar entered the other way round

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase for entered swap places, the second coming first

parts.note: to have entered is to have got in

explanation.surface: Someone came into a pub by the wrong door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; it is a block of metal. The words, not the letters, swap.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast block of gold or other metal is called a bar.

clue.text: Dash, going to back of beyond for this large beast

parts.note: dash as in flair or style is elan

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Rushing to the back of beyond to find some big animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This African antelope is the largest of its kind, so a large beast.

clue.text: Hugo's heroine leads man endlessly astray without hesitation

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jumbled letters surround the hesitation
going astray means wandering off course, so the letters are jumbled
without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A Victor Hugo heroine confidently leads a man off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' scrambles LEADS plus MA into ESMALDA; 'without' means outside, wrapping it round the hesitation. She is the dancer in The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.
explanation.definitionFit: The gypsy dancer in Victor Hugo's novel The Hunchback of Notre-Dame is its heroine.

clue.text: Very different Europeans getting a role?

parts.note: Poles are people from Poland
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: Some Europeans landing an acting job.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes things as far removed as the two ends of the earth, completely unlike.

clue.text: Tailless mammal in covered walkway

indicators.note: without a tail, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a stoat is a small weasel-like mammal

explanation.surface: An animal missing its tail turns up in a cloister.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical Greek architecture a colonnaded portico or roofed walkway was so named.

clue.text: Team player perhaps who's through defending 'donkey'

indicators.note: defending means surrounding protectively, so the word for through goes round the animal

parts.note: per means through or by means of, as in per post
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A footballer who is shielding a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: In football or rugby a player who distributes the ball to teammates is an example.

clue.text: Late leader's work on plant

parts.note: the late person is deceased, dead
a leader is a head; the apostrophe s stands for is, linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A deceased chief's labours at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory; it is a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners remove spent blooms from a plant to encourage more flowering.

clue.text: Crazy fellows dumping maidens in port

indicators.note: dumping means discarding, so the letters for the maidens are thrown out

parts.note: madmen are crazy fellows
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over; two maidens give two Ms

explanation.surface: Lunatics leaving young women behind at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: This city in Yemen is a major seaport on the Gulf of its own name.

clue.text: Vehicles stop, regularly taking in Surrey town

parts.note: cars are vehicles
to halt is to stop
on in the sense of continuing, happening as a regular fixture, as in the show is on every week

explanation.surface: Traffic halts on a regular basis in a commuter town.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog and its readers found the ON loose; it is read as 'on' meaning regularly happening. CARSHALTON is a suburb in south London, historically in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: This place in the London Borough of Sutton was historically part of the county of Surrey.

clue.text: Lovely to include a rich cake halved in trifle

indicators.note: to include means to hold inside, so the beauty's word encloses the rest

parts.note: a lovely is a beautiful woman, a belle

indicators.note: halved means only half of the cake's word survives, so its second half is dropped

parts.note: a gateau is a rich cream cake

explanation.surface: A pretty dessert with rich cake cut in half in a sherry trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' looks like a pudding but means a thing of little importance. GATEAU halved gives GAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinket or something of little value or importance is a trifle.

clue.text: Investigator's work for US singer

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
Bing Crosby was an American crooner

explanation.surface: A detective's job is done on behalf of an American vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Detailed inquiry and questioning is what a detective or researcher does.

clue.text: Bending double almost hurt

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a twin is a double, a lookalike
to sting is to hurt

explanation.surface: Someone stooping over, nearly doubled up in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning or curving out of shape is a synonym for flexing, as a wire does.

clue.text: Handel oratorio I slam, being a South Pacific person

parts.note: Solomon is an oratorio by Handel
to slam is to criticise harshly, to slander

explanation.surface: A critic panning a Handel work, and he happens to live in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the archipelago east of Papua New Guinea is a Pacific islander.

clue.text: Just about noble lying in state

indicators.note: lying in means placed inside, so the nobleman goes within the state

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York state
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A dead aristocrat lying in state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying in state' suggests a body on display, but 'lying in' is the placement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost or very close to is the meaning of the adverbial phrase in the clue.

clue.text: A comedian rocked part of Europe

indicators.note: rocked means shaken about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A comic shook up a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: This Balkan region, and now the country of North Macedonia, lies in south-east Europe.

clue.text: Doctor repeatedly set about opening of surgery in directory

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the doubled time-traveller surrounds the letter
repeatedly says the word is used twice

parts.note: Doctor Who is the BBC television time-lord, so Doctor gives who

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A GP keeps setting about opening a surgery listed in a directory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' puts S between WHO and WHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference book listing notable people and their details is a kind of directory.

clue.text: Followers, hard working around French town

indicators.note: around means the other pieces go either side of the town

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
on means working, as a machine that is on
Angers is a town on the Loire in France

explanation.surface: Diligent supporters working near a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the pair of pieces round the town: hard comes before it and working after.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophantic hangers-around who attach themselves to someone important are followers.

clue.text: Great Dane barking in outdoor cafe

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A large dog yapping in an open-air cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor area where tea and refreshments are served is an open-air cafe.

clue.text: Right away, pick up rubbish that gives complaint

indicators.note: away means removed, so the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it
trash is rubbish

explanation.surface: Collecting litter right away to avoid grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' means a medical ailment, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment, and prickly skin irritation from overheating is one.

clue.text: One terribly boring fat man?

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the scrambled letters go inside the fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is extremely dull and overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges One into EON; 'boring' looks like dull but means drilling into the fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so the question mark marks it as an example of a man.

clue.text: Most flexible essay is cut in literature

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the trimmed essay goes within the literature letters
cut means removed, so the word is is taken out of the essay

parts.note: a thesis is a long essay

explanation.surface: A very supple essay gets trimmed in a literature course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes IS from THESIS to leave THES.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple or most agile is the superlative of the adjective for nimble and bendy.

clue.text: Material fine a real friend gets reduced

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: gets reduced means made shorter, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a brick is a dependable friend in old-fashioned British slang

explanation.surface: A good friend gets a discount on some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'brick' is old British slang for a loyal, reliable friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Woven cloth or textile is called material.
